body:
Autoregressive language models produce, at every prediction step, a vocabulary-sized logit vector whose structure determines the conditional next-token distribution. We empirically identify that the ordered vocabulary-head logits follow a remarkably consistent log-linear relation

\[ z(r) μ- α r. \] across prediction contexts, architectures, and scales, emerging progressively during pretraining. To our knowledge, this is the first systematic analysis of the logit geometry underlying the distributional assumptions used in the prior decoding work. While controlled order-statistic baselines spanning bounded, light-tailed, and heavier-tailed distributions can largely explain the observed log-linear geometry, they do not explain the systematic shift in the slope α: trained language models exhibit α 1.4--1.7, sitting well above the initialization baseline (α 0.2) . Moreover, α correlates with predictive performance, suggesting that it captures learned structure beyond generic extreme-value effects.
summaryZh: 本文对自回归语言模型的Logit几何结构进行了系统性分析。研究发现，词表头Logit遵循一致的对数线性关系，且该结构在预训练过程中逐渐形成。通过对比不同架构与规模的模型，作者指出训练后的模型在斜率参数上表现出显著的规律性偏移，且该偏移与模型预测性能高度相关。这一发现不仅揭示了模型学习到的深层结构，也为优化解码策略提供了理论依据。
